title: Language detection for runtime shader errors not working
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: 4.6.dev 7ed0b6167 ### System information Godot v4.6.dev (7ed0b6167) - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8180) - AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 63.11 GiB memory ### Issue description When a runtime shader error is logged in the debugger the source language is wrongly stated as `C++`, it should probably say something like `GDShader` instead I think the reason for this is the following code which tries to detect the language of a source file, but only from registered languages which only contain `GDScript` and `C#`. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7a207b3eaa6ebeb020a83b52467ddcab9ee1ccf4/editor/debugger/script_editor_debugger.cpp#L675-L684 Note: The detection uses the extension of the source file which changes when the script is built-in or unique to a scene and will not be reliable for detecting the source language (at least that's what I found) ### Steps to reproduce - Create a scene with a node to which you can add a shader script - Add a shader script which can't compile like: ``` shader_type spatial; void vertex() { ``` - Run the scene - Now an error with the described issue should be present in the `Debugger` -> `Errors` ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [wrong-language-error.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23853038/wrong-language-error.zip)
